chi-square.def: The statistic $\chi^2 = \sum \frac{(O - E)^2}{E}$, added over every cell of a table of observed ($O$) and expected ($E$) counts. It is 0 when the observed counts match the expected counts exactly and grows as they move apart.

homogeneity.def: A chi-square test of whether one categorical variable has the same distribution in several populations or treatment groups, using separate random samples or randomly assigned groups. $H_0$: the distributions are the same.

independence-test.def: A chi-square test of whether two categorical variables are associated in a population, using one random sample classified by both variables. $H_0$: there is no association between the variables.

expected-count.def: The count a cell of a two-way table would have, on average, if the null hypothesis were true: $\frac{\text{row total} \times \text{column total}}{\text{grand total}}$. The observed count is the count in the data.
